title: What's the Matter with Kitty?
subtitle: States of matter with Cindy and Dad

sentences.text: Dad hung a small white object on the wall.
"What is that?" I asked.
"It's a mothball, Cindy. There is a chemical inside called naphthalene. It keeps bad smells away," he responded.
Days later, I looked and saw nothing in the mothball.
"Where is the naphthalene? Did Kitty eat it?" I thought.
I couldn't find Kitty.
I was worried.
"Dad, I think Kitty ate the naphthalene. She is probably sick somewhere," I said in tears.
"Oh, dear! Don't cry. Kitty couldn't reach it on the wall. Besides, naphthalene dissolves naturally," he said.
"Naturally?" I responded.
"Yes. The naphthalene became gas. It's called sublimation. Let me show you something," he said.
He brought some ice cubes from the fridge and started heating them in a pan.
"Cindy, watch what happens," he pointed at the ice cubes.
"They melted and became water," I said quietly.
"Yes. If you continue heating the water, it will dry out," he responded.

sentences.text: "The water is gone! It became a gas. That's interesting!" I said.
"It's called evaporation. If you leave a glass of water open, the same thing happens. Do you know water can become a solid, too?" he asked.

chunks.text: If you leave a glass of water open,
Do you know water can become a solid, too?"

sentences.text: "Um, if I leave water in the freezer, it will get frozen and become ice. The water will become a solid!" I snapped my fingers.

chunks.text: if I leave water in the freezer,
it will get frozen and become ice.
The water will become a solid!"

sentences.text: "That's right, Cindy! As you see, matter can change states," he said.
"Thanks Dad. I learned something new today," I responded.
Just then, Kitty came into the room.
I ran and hugged Kitty.
"Where were you, Kitty? I was worried about you," I said.
"I'm so happy you didn't eat the naphthalene after all."

vocabulary.easyEnglish: to put a thing at a high place
vocabulary.easyEnglishLong: When you hang something, you put it up high on a wall or a hook so it stays there.
examples: I always hang my coat on the wall.

comic.meaning: to put a thing up high

panels.caption: Kibu's coat is down on the floor.
Kibu reaches up to the high hook.
Kibu hangs the coat way up high.
Now the coat hangs on the wall!

vocabulary.easyEnglish: a small ball that keeps moths away from clothes
vocabulary.easyEnglishLong: A mothball is a small white ball. People keep it near clothes so hungry bugs stay away.
vocabulary.simpleKo: 옷에서 벌레를 쫓는 작은 흰 공
examples: She has mothballs in her closet.

comic.meaning: a ball that keeps moths away

panels.caption: A hungry moth flies to the clothes!
Kibu sets a white mothball beside them.
Its smell makes the moth fly far away.
The mothball keeps the clothes safe!

vocabulary.easyEnglish: a thing made by changing or mixing
vocabulary.easyEnglishLong: A chemical is a new thing made when other things change or mix together.
examples: Some gardeners use chemicals to kill insects.

panels.caption: Kibu has two different liquids.
Kibu mixes them together. Pop!
A brand-new chemical appears!
A chemical is made by changing things!

vocabulary.easyEnglish: a strong-smelling thing used in mothballs
vocabulary.easyEnglishLong: Naphthalene is the strong-smelling chemical inside a mothball. Its smell keeps bugs away.

panels.caption: Kibu sniffs the small white ball.
Pew! The smell is very, very strong!
That strong smell is naphthalene.
Naphthalene keeps the bugs far away!

vocabulary.easyEnglish: to slowly disappear into a liquid
vocabulary.easyEnglishLong: When something dissolves, it mixes into a liquid and slowly disappears, like sugar in water.
examples: The sugar dissolved in her coffee.

panels.caption: Kibu drops sugar into the water.
Round and round Kibu stirs it.
The sugar melts away into the water.
All gone! The sugar dissolved.

vocabulary.easyEnglish: the changing of a solid into a gas
vocabulary.easyEnglishLong: Sublimation is when a solid turns straight into a gas, with no liquid in between.
examples: Sublimation makes solids change into gases.

comic.meaning: a solid changing into a gas

panels.caption: Kibu sees a hard, cold solid.
It floats straight up as gas!
It skips water! Solid right to gas.
Solid to gas is called sublimation!

vocabulary.easyEnglishLong: When you heat something, you make it hot, like warming a pan over a fire.
examples: I heated the oil in the frying pan.

panels.caption: Kibu has a cold, cold pan.
Kibu heats it over the fire.
The pan turns super, super hot.
Heat makes everything hot!

vocabulary.easyEnglish: to change from a liquid into a solid because of cold
vocabulary.easyEnglishLong: When water freezes, the cold turns it into hard, solid ice.
examples: The water in the lake freezes and turns into ice.

comic.meaning: liquid turns to solid in the cold

panels.caption: Kibu has a glass of cool water.
Kibu makes it freezing, freezing cold.
The water hardens into solid ice.
Freezing turns water into a solid!

comprehensionChecks.question: Frozen water becomes what?
comprehensionChecks.answerText: it will get frozen and become ice.

panels.caption: Kibu is a migrant cat in a new town.
A music show sparks Kibu's interest.
A bossy raccoon forced Kibu to carry boxes.
Old apples begin to rot in the hot shed.
The tired helpers start a strike for fairness.
Kibu asks for respect for every helper.
At last, Kibu can perform on the bright stage.
Kibu and the helpers become heroes of the festival.

wordExplanations.forced: Forced means someone made you do something.
wordExplanations.heroes: Heroes are people who do brave or helpful things.
wordExplanations.interest: Interest means you want to know more about something.
wordExplanations.perform: Perform means to sing, dance, act, or show something in front of people.
wordExplanations.migrant: A migrant is someone who moves to a new place to live or work.
wordExplanations.respect: Respect means treating someone kindly and fairly.
wordExplanations.rot: Rot means to become old, bad, and spoiled.
wordExplanations.strike: A strike is when workers stop working to ask for fair treatment.
